'''Craig Moritz''' is an Australian [[biologist]] and [[evolutionary biologist]] known for his research in evolutionary biology, biogeography and conservation.

== Career ==

During his doctoral studies at the [[Australian National University]] (1980–1985), Moritz demonstrated the existence of [[parthenogenesis]] in the gecko ''[[Heteronotia binoei]]''. He subsequently undertook postdoctoral research at the [[University of Michigan]] from 1985 to 1988 and at the [[University of Queensland]] from 1988 to 2000. From 2000 to 2012, he was director of the [[Museum of Vertebrate Zoology]] and a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="ARC">{{cite web |title=Professor Craig Moritz |url=http://www.arc.gov.au/media/fl11/pdf/Craig%20_Moritz_bio.pdf |publisher=Australian Research Council |access-date=15 October 2026}}</ref> In 2012, he became a professor in the Division of Evolution, Ecology and Genetics at the Australian National University.<ref name="ANU">{{cite web |title=Moritz Lab – Evolutionary Biogeography & Conservation |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=http%3A%2F%2Fbiology.anu.edu.au%2Fcraig_moritz%2F |publisher=Australian National University |via=Wikiwix |access-date=15 October 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==

Moritz's research spans [[evolutionary biology]], [[molecular ecology]], [[biogeography]], [[conservation biology]], [[speciation]], parthenogenesis in [[lizard]]s and [[phylogeography]].<ref name="ARC"/> He has contributed to the description and classification of several animal taxa, particularly Australian [[gecko]]s, as well as [[amphibian]]s.<ref name="ARC"/>

Taxa associated with his taxonomic work include:

* ''[[Amazophrynella]]''<ref name="Amazophrynella">{{cite web |title=Amphibian Species of the World: Amazophrynella |url=https://amphibiansoftheworld.amnh.org/ |publisher=American Museum of Natural History |access-date=15 October 2026}}</ref>
* ''[[Saltuarius]]''<ref name="Saltuarius">{{cite web |title=Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) |url=http://www.cbif.gc.ca/pls/itisca/next?taxa=&p_format=&p_ifx=&p_lang=fr&v_tsn=818082 |publisher=Canadian Biodiversity Information Facility |access-date=15 October 2026}}</ref>
* ''[[Phyllurus isis]]''<ref name="ReptileDatabase">{{cite web |title=The Reptile Database |url=https://reptile-database.reptarium.cz/ |access-date=15 October 2026}}</ref>
* ''[[Phyllurus nepthys]]''<ref name="ReptileDatabase"/>
* ''[[Phyllurus ossa]]''<ref name="ReptileDatabase"/>
* ''[[Orraya occultus]]''<ref name="ReptileDatabase"/>

== Awards and honours ==

In 2012, Moritz became an Australian Research Council Laureate Fellow. He has also been associated with the [[California Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="ARC"/>

The gecko species ''[[Saltuarius moritzi]]'', described in 2008, was named in his honour in recognition of his contributions to the phylogenetics of Australian rainforest reptiles.<ref name="SaltuariusMoritzi">{{cite web |title=Saltuarius moritzi |url=https://reptile-database.reptarium.cz/ |publisher=The Reptile Database |access-date=15 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="Beolens2011">{{cite book |last1=Beolens |first1=Bo |last2=Watkins |first2=Michael |last3=Grayson |first3=Michael |title=The Eponym Dictionary of Reptiles |publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press |year=2011 |pages=1–296}}</ref> The gecko ''[[Gehyra moritzi]]'' was also named in his honour.
